study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities unveil two major depressive disorder subtypes with contrasting abnormal patterns of abnormality

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Identify MDD subtypes using individualized deviations in resting-state functional connectivity by comparing each subject's edges to normative ranges derived from healthy controls via tolerance intervals, and evaluate reproducibility and clinical relevance.

rci3_hc_age.reason: The paper provides mean and standard deviation for HC age (36.15 ± 24.55 years) but does not report the minimum and maximum values. The SD appears unusually large (24.55), which may indicate a wide age range, but actual range is not specified. Note: Table 1 shows MDD age SD as 14.62, suggesting the 24.55 in the text may be a typographical error, but I report what is explicitly stated for HCs in the text.
rci3_hc_age.supporting_text: These data include rsfMRI data from 25 research sites, comprising 1276 MDD patients (mean age: 36.23 ± 21.38 years, 63.71% females) and 1104 HCs (mean age: 36.15 ± 24.55 years, 58.06% females).

rci4_hc_sex.reason: The paper provides the total number of HCs (1104) and the number of males (463) in Table 1. The number of females was calculated by subtracting the number of males from the total (1104 - 463 = 641). The percentages were calculated from these counts.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two robust MDD subtypes show opposite-signed, widespread rsFC abnormalities relative to HCs; subtypes markedly improve case-control discriminability and are reproducible across subsampling, leave-one-site-out, parameter changes, and in untreated patients; patterns differ from schizophrenia.
